This script defines the class of each variable in the dataset.

### 1. Load required libraries

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
```

### 2. Import the dataset

Load the Covidence dataset

```{r}

source(here("code/cleanData.R"))

#this is not working in the script, but works in the console.
#Need to work out why
#d <- cleanData()

```

Load the data dictionary

```{r}

dict <- read_csv(here("data/data_dictionary.csv"))

```

### 3. Update variable types in `d` to what we want indicated in `dict$Type`

Merge the data dictionary with the dataset

```{r}
# Create a named vector to map column types
type_mapping <- setNames(dict$Type, dict$`Short column name`)

# Filter type_mapping to include only columns present in `d`
type_mapping <- type_mapping[names(type_mapping) %in% names(d)]

# Function to safely convert columns
convert_column <- function(column, type) {
  if (type == "numeric") {
    suppressWarnings(parse_number(column))
  } else if (type == "character") {
    parse_character(column)
  } else if (type == "logical") {
    parse_logical(column)
  } else if (type == "integer") {
    suppressWarnings(parse_integer(column))
  } else if (type == "factor") {
    parse_factor(column)
  } else {
    column # Leave unchanged if the type isn't specified
  }
}

# Apply the conversion based on type mapping
d <- d %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(names(type_mapping)), 
    ~ convert_column(.x, type_mapping[cur_column()])
  ))
     
```
